messages:
Alex M.: Quick follow-up on the prefix/KV RFC — proposal below for a lighter-weight sharing mode to avoid eviction cascade risk when tenants have wildly different hotness.

Alex M.: TL;DR: add an opt-in 'lite-sharing' contract where small prefixes (<N keys or <M bytes) can be shared across tenants but use per-tenant eviction credits and strict demote fences. This keeps the throughput benefits of sharing without the credit spillover correctness hazards.

Priya S.: Hmm curious — what's the trigger for falling back to isolated mode? on-credit-exhaust or based on observed tail latency per tenant?

Alex M.: Two triggers planned: (1) per-tenant credit drop below threshold (fast), (2) sustained 95th latency uplift for >30s (slow). Both are config knobs.

Marco G.: I ran a quick sim — sharing helps cold-start hit-rate for small tails, but when a hot tenant spikes it steals eviction budget and pushes others out. With the lite-sharing rules I simulated, tail latency regressions drop from ~18% to ~2% in mixed workloads. Link to sim: https://go/reports/prefetch-lite-sim (internal)

Jin W.: Race concern: if we demote a prefix concurrently while another node is doing a handoff, we can end up double-evicting and lose residency accounting. Any ideas to keep demote handshake idempotent?

Taylor R.: We discussed using a short-lived demote token (uuid + epoch) that is CAS'd into the prefix descriptor. Handoff checks token; if mismatch treat as noop. That makes demote idempotent and observable.

Alex M.: Exactly. token lifecycle: create -> publish -> wait for ack windows -> finalize. If a node sees a stale token it aborts.

Priya S.: Can we avoid long blocking during publish wait? we don't want to stall reads.

Taylor R.: Publish is async. readers check current token; if pending they proceed with a guarded read path that avoids creating new residency entries. Only the handoff/finalize path updates residency.

Jin W.: Still worried about inflight prefetches: they may re-add the prefix after demote. Need a fast grace window that rejects re-prefetch from non-owner for X ms.

Alex M.: Proposal: after finalize we set a transient tombstone with TTL = grace_ms. Prefetches from other nodes see tombstone and obey a reject-backoff.

Marco G.: That matches sim variant C where grace_ms=200ms eliminated the double-add flapping we saw.

cache-bot: perf-tests/prefetch-lite/2026-03-20 completed. Summary: 1200 iters, mixed-tenancy, median latency neutral, 95p improved vs baseline. Artifacts: https://ci/cache-tests/1759001234

Priya S.: Config example? would help on ops side.

Alex M.: Sure — sample config snippet:
```
prefix_sharing:
  mode: lite
  max_shared_prefix_bytes: 65536
  max_shared_prefix_keys: 128
  tenant_credit_threshold: 0.15
  demote_grace_ms: 200
  fallback_on_latency_pct: 95
  fallback_window_s: 30
```

Taylor R.: Implementation notes: API changes limited — add Mode enum + token field on PrefixDescriptor. Runtime behavior lives in prefetch manager and demote/finalize flows. We should gate behind feature flag and gradual rollout.

Marco G.: Ops: we need new telemetry: per-prefix ownership transitions, token mismatches, grace tombstone rejections, and per-tenant credit drains. Add heatmap for cross-tenant eviction collisions.

Jin W.: For correctness doc: add a short proof sketch that demote + token CAS + tombstone prevents double-residency within the grace window and that credits are conserved under eventual completion. I'll draft it.

Alex M.: Great. Action items:
- Jin: draft correctness sketch + edgecases (due EOD Fri).
- Taylor: implement token + tombstone scaffold in prefetch manager (feature flag) — PR draft by mid-week.
- Marco: run mixed-tenant sim with traffic spikes and validate grace_ms choices (iterating).
- Priya: update ops runbook and config schema example.

Priya S.: +1 to action items. Also suggest adding a small canary that routes 1% of traffic to lite-sharing to ensure no regressions.

Alex M.: Agreed — canary + metrics gates. I'll open RFC follow-up PR that includes design + config + rollout plan.

Taylor R.: One more note: keep the default for max_shared_prefix_bytes small (64KB) so we don't accidentally share large prefix blobs. Ops can increase per-tenant when they opt in.

Marco G.: Sounds good. I'll start the sim runs and post numbers here.

Alex M.: Thanks all. If no blockers, we'll try to get the PR in by next week and start canarying. :rocket:
